newsitem.title: USA: About $1 bln U.S. corp bond issues to test market.
newsitem.headline: About $1 bln U.S. corp bond issues to test market.

text.p: The expected issuance of about $1 billion of high-grade U.S. corporate debt Wednesday has captured the attention of players looking for signs of investor appetites amid rising rates, dealers said.

The new issues, led by $500 million of seven-year notes from Philip Morris Cos Inc, are a "test" to the market, which has been devoid of significant deals since the onset of stock and bond market malaise last week, the dealers said.
Uncertainty over the success of the new issues was widespread; syndicate officials were reluctant to make predictions about the outcome.
There was one positive sign in the ailing high-yield market -- reports of better bids for Tuesday's $75 million Tekni-Plex Inc.
In investment grades, dealers said the market has not been deluged with selling but a clear dearth of buying has heightened the uncertainty for issuance.

"We need to monitor what's going to happen with these new issues to see what's going on out there," said one syndicate official at a large Midwestern securities firm. "We've had the same thing going on for the past couple years -- with stocks and bonds backing up -- and every time it has paid issuers to wait for lower levels...the bond market has come back and the stock market has gone to new highs."

Other new issues include Noble Affiliates's $350 million in 30- and 100-year bonds via Morgan Stanley & Co Inc/UBS Securities, and $100 million in 100-year bonds from Amgen Inc via Morgan Stanley/Merrill Lynch & Co Inc.

The Philip Morris bonds, to be priced via Goldman, Sachs & Co, may be priced at a spread of 75 basis points over Treasuries. That level was considered "the right offer" by one industrials trader not associated with the selling group.

In the high-yield market, talk of a 101 bid for the par-priced Tekni-Plex issue was mildly comforting, traders said, but activity was still termed sloppy. The list of deals postponed this week was extended on Wednesday as $75 million Radio One senior subordinated notes was removed from the private placement calendar for next week, according to a market source.
Separately, sources said Ramsay Health Care Inc's $75 million seven-year senior note deal is questionable.
"Issuers like Ramsay who don't need to tap the market now may decide to wait it out," a syndicate source said. "Also the bank-loan market is very hot and issuers may look to bank loans instead."

A $150 million issue of 10-year senior subordinated debt from Sterling Chemicals Inc STX.N, expected Tuesday, priced this morning as 11-1/4s to yield 11-1/2 percent or 462 basis points over Treasuries via Credit Suisse First Boston.

Other junk bond issues still on for this week include $100 million 10-year senior notes from Bellwether Exploration Co and $80 million seven-year senior notes from Prime Matrix Wireless Communications via J.P. Morgan Securities. Also, Urohealth Systems Inc may issue $100 million seven-year senior subordinated notes through a Bear Stearns & Co group.
